overview.title: From setup to evaluation.
overview.subtitle: Source-backed capability areas
overview.footnote: Configuration guide: setup, behavior, requirements, and limitations.

exempt_components.reason: Application assembly supports host-owned session capabilities rather than owning a separate product capability.
The local IPC client is transport infrastructure for session and task capabilities.
The detached process boundary serves harness capabilities and owns no competing product behavior.
The executor is the isolated backend for workspace execution and verification capabilities.
Headless JSONL is a projection of the same session and task capabilities.
Browser review is included in the sessions, review, and reflection capability owned by the authoritative harness.

capabilities.title: Configuration, authentication, and skills
capabilities.summary: Loads bounded local configuration and credentials, dispatches login/status/logout, admits durable sessions, and exposes refreshed skill metadata and bodies through the host context service.

persistence.anchor: pub fn logout_chatgpt(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<bool, AuthError>

limitations: Skills are disabled by default and are reference data rather than task authority.
Environment API keys are not persisted; ChatGPT credentials use the shared Codex auth file, so logout signs both Orvek and Codex out.

capabilities.title: Installation updates
capabilities.summary: Routes source and Cargo installations to the matching Cargo command, defers externally managed binaries to their package manager, and replaces release-archive binaries only after release, checksum, and signature verification.
limitations: No Orvek crate or signed macOS binary release is published yet; current source installations receive a Cargo install command instead of a release-archive update.

capabilities.title: Durable completion hooks
capabilities.summary: Pins a configured host shell notification before each task request, delivers it after terminal task settlement, and journals intent, claim, and result so restart recovery resumes only unclaimed effects.

entrypoints.anchor: pub async fn serve(host: Arc<Host>, shutdown: CancellationToken) -> io::Result<()>

limitations: Hooks cover terminal task outcomes only; conversation-only turns, auxiliary requests, local shell submissions, and requests rejected before a task exists do not notify.

The command runs on the host through /bin/sh even for sandbox tasks. A claimed effect without a recorded result remains unknown and is not automatically retried; arbitrary shell effects are not exactly once.

capabilities.title: Sessions, review, and reflection
capabilities.summary: Resumes and forks host-owned sessions, projects them into the terminal, serves frozen browser review data with recorded feedback, and runs reflection as non-mutating auxiliary work.

entrypoints.anchor: The detached host owns all work.

limitations: Browser review requires separately installed web assets for source builds.
The terminal opens at most one fork pane at a time; reflection records an auxiliary report and cannot mutate task or workspace authority.

capabilities.title: Session handoff
capabilities.summary: Runs a dedicated auxiliary handoff report after work settles, then creates a fresh-history host context at the same stable workspace checkpoint and retains the continuation draft when creation is uncertain.

dispatchers.anchor: async fn create(client: &HostClient, parent: SessionCursor) -> Result<SessionView>

documentation.anchor: ## Hand off to a fresh context

limitations: Handoff requires a settled workspace checkpoint and aborts if the task or workspace changes while the auxiliary report runs.
The new context keeps the workspace checkpoint but starts with empty provider history; a failed or uncertain creation retains the generated draft and may require resuming the reported context ID.

capabilities.title: Legacy-session import
capabilities.summary: Discovers bounded historical SQLite sessions, snapshots selected lineage and resume bytes without mutating the source, and commits provenance-backed native host contexts idempotently.
limitations: Import is bounded to a 64 MiB source snapshot, 10,000 sessions, 100,000 records, 32 MiB selected bytes, and 30 seconds; unsupported or corrupt historical schemas and lineage are rejected.

The original database is never migrated or deleted and may retain unredacted history. Imported tool calls, instructions, and completion events are historical provenance only and cannot grant authority or certificates.

capabilities.title: Multimodal image submission
capabilities.summary: Pastes clipboard images into terminal drafts, stores media as bounded content-addressed artifacts, restores persisted drafts, and reconstructs ordered provider image parts at the submission boundary.
limitations: A submission accepts at most eight images and 4 MiB of decoded image bytes in total.
Only embedded base64 PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP data with matching signatures are admitted; file and network URLs are rejected.
New-task and ordinary submissions still require a textual objective; image-only task requests are rejected by durable admission.
Provider or model image support is not preflighted, and images are provider context rather than files mounted into the native workspace or sandbox.

capabilities.title: Local and remote memory
capabilities.summary: Stores bounded evidence-backed memory locally or remotely and exposes explicit scan, read, mutation, lesson, and transfer operations.

persistence.anchor: pub async fn export<S: MemoryStore>(store: &S, directory: &Path) -> Result<Self, MemoryError>

limitations: Memory is disabled by default, unencrypted locally, and unavailable to delegated children.
Explicit export, import, push, and pull use the local store from any directory and ignore memory.enabled and workspace scope; remote transfer still requires configured credentials.

capabilities.title: Context projection and exact retrieval
capabilities.summary: Derives stable and live provider context from authoritative history, selects measured representations, and preserves exact source retrieval.
limitations: Bitmap selection depends on comparable provider receipts and falls back to native text when evidence is missing.

capabilities.title: Isolated subagents
capabilities.summary: Runs bounded read-only child model sessions with session-scoped management, durable lifecycle records, and schema-validated results.
limitations: Children require the Docker runtime, are read-only, share a live workspace, and cannot delegate recursively.

capabilities.title: Sloppiness diagnostics
capabilities.summary: Measures deterministic source growth, duplication, redundant Rust forms, and complexity hotspots without treating metrics as completion evidence.
limitations: Only Rust has AST-aware redundancy and complexity analysis; the report is not a quality score.

capabilities.title: Terminal performance
capabilities.summary: Caches transcript wrapping, syntax styles, and layout work while scheduling bounded rendering around input and streaming updates.
limitations: Local rendering benchmarks do not measure provider latency or task success.

capabilities.title: Evaluation tooling
capabilities.summary: Provides the Harbor adapter, SnapCompact paired runs and accounting, read-only context-cost analysis, deterministic context-transition fixtures, and incident-replay task generation, scoring, and result analysis. These tools preserve explicit unknowns but do not establish live-model quality or benchmark qualification.

dispatchers.anchor: def analyze(document: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:

limitations: Harbor and live SnapCompact trials require external providers, credentials, and local Docker; the Harbor Docker execution path is documented as not validated for Orvek 0.1.0.
The SnapCompact runner does not implement the fork case, host-mode tasks cannot provide the required settled fork checkpoint, and missing usage or receipts remain unknown rather than zero.
Context-cost output is descriptive; its 3.7x input counterfactual is not a billed value or an Orvek savings claim.

Context transitions are default-disabled and have deterministic wiring evidence only; live-model quality and full-cost acceptance remain pending. The sandbox verifier additionally requires Docker and ORVEK_EXECUTOR_HELPER.

Incident replay is an incident-inspired proxy, not Anthropic's environment and not a direct Mythos-rate comparison. It has an embedded deterministic verifier but no dedicated README or focused generator/analyzer contract test.
The checked-in 2026-09-19 SnapCompact report is historical legacy evidence and is intentionally not cited as current persistence or qualification proof.

capabilities.title: Portable trace bundles and offline replay
capabilities.summary: Exports a pinned journal prefix and bounded artifact closure, then replays reducers and receipt relationships without executing tools or providers.
limitations: Replay verifies recorded state and supported causal links; it does not rerun tools or authenticate a wholesale rewritten bundle.

capabilities.title: Experimental online trace re-execution
capabilities.summary: Extracts only original task intent from a trace bundle and submits it through a fresh headless host run with new identities, provider calls, tool effects, and evidence.

entrypoints.anchor: pub(crate) async fn reexecute(self, config: &Config) -> Result<()>

dispatchers.anchor: pub(crate) async fn reexecute(self, config: &Config) -> Result<()>

limitations: The command requires --experimental and a new empty workspace; it is online execution, not offline replay.
Only original intent is reused. New provider and tool calls may incur cost and side effects, and no historical certificate, evidence, identity, or receipt is inherited.

capabilities.title: Optional interpreter for composed tool calls
capabilities.summary: Runs bounded QuickJS cells that compose only the tools admitted to the current request and retain explicit artifact-backed checkpoints.
limitations: The interpreter has no ambient filesystem, process, network, credential, or module-loader access.

capabilities.title: Durable event intake and management
capabilities.summary: Lets a same-user CLI register, inspect, deliver to, cancel, and disable event sources; the host durably deduplicates receipts and runs latest-only interval scheduling against existing session authority.

entrypoints.anchor: pub(crate) async fn run(self, config: &Config) -> Result<()>

dispatchers.anchor: pub(crate) async fn query(&self, command: Command) -> Result<Response>
pub async fn event_source(&self, source: Uuid) -> Result<SourceRecord, HostError>
pub async fn event(&self, source: Uuid, key: &str) -> Result<EventRecord, HostError>

limitations: This is a same-user Unix-socket webhook adapter, not an HTTP server and not per-source authentication.

Payloads are untrusted UTF-8 task data; they cannot create sessions, select workspaces, change profiles, grant capabilities, or switch execution modes, but native execution still retains the user's broad host authority.
Payloads are limited to 64 KiB, source configuration to 256 KiB, objectives to 16 KiB, and keys to 1–256 UTF-8 bytes.
The host allows 64 enabled sources and 128 outstanding event records; deduplication records currently have no expiry.
A successful delivery response proves durable receipt, not successful task completion.

capabilities.title: Trace monitoring and native-read management
capabilities.summary: Runs a bounded host-side journal monitor and lets a same-user CLI report status, change sampling, install one versioned native-read reply envelope, and roll back to the retained previous envelope.

entrypoints.anchor: pub(crate) async fn run(self, config: &Config) -> Result<()>

dispatchers.anchor: pub(crate) async fn query(&self, command: Command) -> Result<Response>
pub async fn set_monitor_sampling(&self, every: u32) -> Result<(), HostError>
pub async fn rollback_read_behavior(&self, expected: Digest) -> Result<Digest, HostError>

documentation.anchor: # Trace monitoring and native read recovery

limitations: Monitoring is local deterministic recovery, not general autonomous repair or proof of model quality; it cannot change prompts, tool schemas, repository policy, contracts, binaries, task budgets, or arbitrary code.
Management uses the same-user Unix operator socket; it is not a model tool, event-payload field, or public HTTP API.
Install and rollback affect only new sessions. Existing sessions, forks, and handoffs retain their pinned configuration.
Sampling must be 1–10000; install-read bytes must be 4096–32768; report pages are limited to 1–100 rows.
The worker reads at most 64 journal records per tick and evaluates one candidate at a time. Comparisons remain descriptive and uncertain; no live-model comparison has run.
Warnings are process-local rather than a durable incident log, reports and artifacts can contain private provenance, and no telemetry export or automatic retention deletion is configured.

capabilities.title: Experimental context phase transitions
capabilities.summary: Replaces eligible settled ranges only in the derived context view while retaining exact source history and retrieval authority.
limitations: The feature is disabled by default and model summaries remain derived claims rather than task authority.

capabilities.title: Task admission and execution
capabilities.summary: Admits a host request into one durable task and drives its provider and tool loop through the authoritative controller.
limitations: Native tasks finish without the sandbox verification certificate.

capabilities.title: Durable submission queue and steering
capabilities.summary: Admits idempotent host-owned submissions and applies expected-input-guarded editing, promotion, cancellation, and reordering while one recovery worker consumes durable queue order.
limitations: Edits and moves succeed only while a submission remains queued and its expected input digest still matches; promotion is semantically distinct from reordering.
The queue is bounded to 16 pending submissions per session and 128 across the host. The detached host, not the TUI, owns durable order and recovery.

capabilities.title: Sandbox-only operator shell submissions
capabilities.summary: Accepts a leading-! operator command as a durable manual job, executes it only in the isolated Docker workspace without model inference, and publishes bounded output and adopted workspace state.
limitations: Native-host shell admission is rejected; this path requires the isolated Docker executor.
The command creates no coding task or model history, its output is not automatically sent to the provider, and completion hooks do not run for it.
The TUI supplies a 120-second timeout and 256 KiB output bound; validated protocol maxima are 300 seconds and 1 MiB.

capabilities.title: Workspace tool execution
capabilities.summary: Admits bounded file and command tools against the native workspace or an isolated Docker working copy and records their outcomes.
limitations: Host execution uses the operator's authority and finishes without a verification certificate; protected verification and patch delivery are sandbox-only.

capabilities.title: Verification and reproducible delivery
capabilities.summary: Runs protected checks on frozen candidates, reproduces exact patches, and records a completion certificate only after every obligation is satisfied.
limitations: Certificates cover the declared contract and recorded evidence, not external state that the checks did not observe.
